title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via DNS Rebinding
preconditions: Attacker must convince the user to visit an attacker-controlled domain in a supported browser.
attack_path: User visits attacker.com -> FocusLocker intercepts URL and extracts domain -> FocusLocker's SmartScanUseCase attempts to fetch meta description -> attacker.com DNS returns public IP during validation -> URL.openConnection() resolves DNS again and attacker returns private IP (e.g., 127.0.0.1) -> FocusLocker fetches sensitive internal services on the local network.
impact: Exposes local or private network services to an attacker.
remediation: Disable DNS resolution entirely during validation, or use a custom SocketFactory/HostnameVerifier that pins the validated IP address for the HTTP connection, preventing the secondary DNS lookup.

title: Rate Limiting Bypass on OTP Endpoints via Variable Emails
preconditions: Attacker can send POST requests to the backend API.
attack_path: Attacker writes a script to repeatedly POST to /api/verify-contact with a different email (e.g., test1@example.com, test2@example.com). The rate limiter keys off the email instead of the IP, treating each as a new client and never triggering the block.
impact: Exhausts the email sending quotas and causes Denial of Service (DoS) and potential financial loss.
remediation: Implement a strict IP-based rate limiter for the OTP endpoint that cannot be bypassed, or limit the number of OTP requests per IP globally alongside the email limiter.
